x: Section 2(1)(bc), inserted by the 2015 amendment, defines 'economic boycott' (refusal to deal, work for hire or do business etc.).

x: Section 14: 'For the purpose of providing for speedy trial' the State Government specifies a Court of Session as a Special Court in each district.
source: PoA Act 1989 original text (web: hrw.org/legacy/reports/1999/india/India994-16.htm, Appendix B) s.14

x: Section 3(2)(vii): a public servant who commits any offence under s.3 gets not less than one year, extendable to the punishment for that offence.
source: PoA Act 1989 original text (web: hrw.org/legacy/reports/1999/india/India994-16.htm, Appendix B) s.3(2)(vii)

x: Section 18 PoA Act: s.438 CrPC (anticipatory bail) does not apply to offences under the Act (now BNSS s.482).
source: PoA Act 1989 original text (web: hrw.org/legacy/reports/1999/india/India994-16.htm, Appendix B) s.18

x: Section 23(1): the Central Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (PoA Rules 1995).
source: PoA Act 1989 original text (web: hrw.org/legacy/reports/1999/india/India994-16.htm, Appendix B) s.23

x: Section 14: the State Government specifies the Special Court with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court.
source: PoA Act 1989 original text (web: hrw.org/legacy/reports/1999/india/India994-16.htm, Appendix B) s.14

x: The Special Court can forfeit property (s.7), remove a likely offender from Scheduled/Tribal areas (s.10) and order measurements and photographs (s.12); conferring police powers on another officer is the State Government's power (s.9), not the court's.
source: PoA Act 1989 original text (web: hrw.org/legacy/reports/1999/india/India994-16.htm, Appendix B) s.7, 9, 10, 12

x: The collective fine is imposed by the State Government (s.16, applying PCR s.10A), not by the Special Court; removal (s.10), forfeiture (s.7) and measurements (s.12) are Special Court powers.
source: PoA Act 1989 original text (web: hrw.org/legacy/reports/1999/india/India994-16.htm, Appendix B) s.7, 10, 12, 16

x: The PoA Act has 23 sections (s.23 = power to make rules); amendments added 14A, 15A and 18A without renumbering.
source: PoA Act 1989 original text (web: hrw.org/legacy/reports/1999/india/India994-16.htm, Appendix B) s.1-23

x: Section 6 applies IPC Chapter IV (general exceptions – private defence, trifling harm s.95) to the Act, so those pleas are open; and s.3 covers only accused who are not SC/ST, so 'I belong to the victim's caste' is also a valid plea. Hence none of the pleas is barred.
source: PoA Act 1989 original text (web: hrw.org/legacy/reports/1999/india/India994-16.htm, Appendix B) s.3, s.6
